## Inspect the data

The built-in `iris` dataset contains flower measurements for three species.
This report uses base R, so no additional data or plotting packages are needed.

```{r}
#| label: inspect-data
head(iris)
```

## Summarize petal length

Calculate the mean petal length in centimeters for each species.

```{r}
#| label: summarize-species
aggregate(Petal.Length ~ Species, data = iris, FUN = mean)
```

## Compare measurements

```{r}
#| label: fig-iris
#| fig-cap: "Petal dimensions for the three iris species."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
species_colors <- c("#2563eb", "#d97706", "#059669")
plot(
  iris$Petal.Length,
  iris$Petal.Width,
  col = species_colors[as.integer(iris$Species)],
  pch = 19,
  xlab = "Petal length (cm)",
  ylab = "Petal width (cm)"
)
legend(
  "topleft",
  legend = levels(iris$Species),
  col = species_colors,
  pch = 19,
  bty = "n"
)
```

## What to look for

@fig-iris shows how petal length and width vary across species.
Try changing `Petal.Length` and `Petal.Width` to `Sepal.Length` and
`Sepal.Width`, and update the labels to match.
